reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily provides a beginner tutorial on signing up for Coinbase, connecting a payment method, reviewing a Bitcoin order, and understanding fees. The classroom setting and related tutorial titles support an educational context, while the wealth statement is described as aspirational rather than a specific guarantee and cryptocurrency risks are acknowledged.

opening.argument: The presentation links monetary incentives to concrete viewer actions. The description advertises an “$100 Signup Bonus” for an IRA-related crypto service while directing viewers to an external destination, and the video separately instructs beginners to connect a bank account and purchase Bitcoin. That combination makes the content more than neutral instruction: viewers are given a financial inducement and a ready-made path to act through promoted crypto services.

Preferred Platforms : https://cryptoschool.cc/

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the walkthrough educational does not resolve the solicitation. The cited tutorial language shows viewers how to fund an account and buy crypto, while the description adds an external signup bonus and numerous promoted destinations. The fact that the presenter says a particular purchase is hypothetical does not remove the real-world calls to connect a bank account, register, and use the linked services.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The bonus is listed for a separate IRA-related service, not presented as a guaranteed reward for following the Coinbase tutorial. The speaker explicitly describes the transaction as hypothetical, and the material explains account mechanics rather than promising that viewers will receive money. A link and a signup offer do not show that the advertised reward is deceptive or that Coinbase purchases are required to obtain it.

opening.argument: The risk signals are concentrated in a financial signup funnel. A Coinbase page shown in the video displays “Earn 4.75% APY on USDC” alongside a “Claim free trial” control, while the description directs viewers to multiple crypto exchanges and related services. The video also closes by hoping viewers can make “generational wealth” with crypto. Presenting a specific yield and a wealth outcome beside easy participation cues can make a risky crypto product look like an accessible return opportunity, even though the material does not establish the conditions or limitations behind those claims.

citations.quote: i hope we can all make generational wealth together with crypto
Bonuses, trading rewards & exclusive perks available below
Up to $10,000 a month of purchases, if you're buying crypto every month, you don't have to pay their fees

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes fees and mechanics but leaves the return framing unaddressed. The visible APY and free-trial invitation appear in the same Coinbase presentation as the account walkthrough, and the description packages “bonuses” and “trading rewards” with external crypto services. A disclaimer cannot by itself neutralize a concrete yield display and aspirational wealth message placed next to participation instructions.

citations.quote: Bonuses, trading rewards & exclusive perks available below
i hope we can all make generational wealth together with crypto

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The page display does not prove that viewers are being promised a fixed or passive return from a pool, lending arrangement, or staking program. The speaker explains that cryptocurrency involves risk and volatility, and expressly says the material is not financial advice. The wealth statement is framed as a hope, not a promise, while the tutorial explains how to inspect fees before purchasing.

opening.argument: Although framed as a beginner lesson, the video functions as a promotion for buying crypto. It repeatedly directs viewers through funding an exchange, selecting Bitcoin, reviewing a dollar purchase, and executing it, then ends by associating crypto with “generational wealth.” The description expands that funnel with numerous exchange, IRA, tax, brokerage, and charting links and calls some platforms preferred. This is operational guidance designed to move viewers toward token participation, not merely an impartial explanation of technology.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The classroom-style framing does not change the commercial direction of the material. The defense identifies the steps being taught, but those steps culminate in buying Bitcoin and are surrounded by preferred-platform links and a wealth-oriented closing. Explaining how to execute a purchase can itself be promotional when the presentation repeatedly normalizes token acquisition as the easy route to getting started.

citations.quote: I'm going to show you a very simplistic, step-by-step tutorial on how to do just that.
that is the quickest, fastest way to get started and buy your first Bitcoin

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Instructional detail is not evidence of deceptive promotion. The video explains both buying and selling, describes transaction fees and spreads, distinguishes the exchange from the wallet, and warns that crypto is volatile. The closing hope about wealth does not guarantee appreciation, and the hypothetical $1,000 example does not show that viewers were promised profit or dividends.
